verses.text: So, think of us as Christ's servants and stewards entrusted with God's mysteries.
What matters for a steward is to prove faithful.
It means very little to me if you judge me—or if any human court does. I don't even judge myself.
My conscience is clear, but that doesn't prove I'm in the right. The Lord is the one who judges me.

So don't judge anything before the right time. Wait until the Lord comes. He'll bring hidden things out into the light and reveal what's in people's hearts. Then each person will receive praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I've applied these examples to myself and Apollos for your sake, so you can learn not to go beyond what is written. Then none of you will get arrogant and take sides against one another.
Who made you different from anyone else? What do you have that you didn't receive? And if you received it, why brag as if it were your own achievement?
You already have everything you want! You're already rich! You've started ruling without us. I wish you really were ruling, so we could reign with you!
As I see it, God has put us apostles on display at the end of the procession, like people sentenced to die. We've become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels and to humans.
We're fools for Christ, but you think you're wise in Christ. We're weak, but you are strong. You get honor, while we get disrespect.
Even now we're hungry and thirsty, poorly clothed, beaten, and without a home.
We work hard with our own hands. When people insult us, we bless them; when we're persecuted, we endure.
When people slander us, we answer gently. We've become like the world's trash, the dirt everyone scrapes off—right up to now.
I'm not writing this to embarrass you. I'm warning you as my dearly loved children.
You may have ten thousand guardians in Christ, but you don't have many fathers. In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
So I urge you: imitate me.
That's why I sent Timothy to you. He's my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, and he'll remind you how I live in Christ Jesus, just as I teach in every church everywhere.
Some of you have become arrogant, thinking I won't come to you.
But I'll come soon, if the Lord wills, and then I'll find out not just what these arrogant people say, but what power they have.
God's Kingdom isn't just talk; it's power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?
